title: Fast Models Need Slow Developers — Sarah Chieng, Cerebras
talk_summary: A Cerebras DX lead argues that 20x-faster code models (Codex Spark at 1,200 tok/s vs 40-60 tok/s for Sonnet/Opus) turn verification, refactoring, and multi-candidate generation from expensive to nearly free, but only if developers abandon one-shot mega-prompts and many-unverified-agents habits. The playbook is: slow model plans, fast model executes, cheap validation at every step, and externalized memory files to keep context bounded.

takeaways.what_they_do: Use a large slow model for planning and long-horizon decomposition, then spawn fast cheap models as executors that work the checklist step by step.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use a larger model like GPT 5.4 or 5.3 for your planning or your long horizon workflows and then using a faster model like Codex Spark as your actual executor
takeaways.numbers: Codex Spark 1,200 tok/s vs Sonnet/Opus 40-60 tok/s (~20x)

takeaways.technique: Capture successful sessions as reusable skills
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the hard task once with a strong model, capture the working trajectory as a skill, then have a small fast model replay it repeatedly in the background.
takeaways.evidence_quote: use a model like GPT 5.4 to actually have it do the initial harder larger task, capture that as a skill, and therefore making it a verifiable repeatable workflow

takeaways.technique: Validation at every step, not at the end
takeaways.what_they_do: Because fast inference makes checks near-instant, run test suites, linting, pre-commit hooks, diff reviews, and browser QA after each step rather than once before push.
takeaways.evidence_quote: at 1,200 tokens per second, a model like Codex Spark makes validation basically free ... Test suites, linting, pre-commit hooks, diff reviews, browser-based QA automations

takeaways.what_they_do: Generate many variants (e.g. 15 per agent, 75 total) in the time one used to take, then have a human or reviewer pick the best, inducing 'taste' into output.
takeaways.evidence_quote: generate 15 versions in the same time that it would have taken the a previous model generate one version, and I can cherry pick the version that I like the best
takeaways.numbers: 15 versions per agent; 5 agents x 15 = 75 candidates

takeaways.what_they_do: Persist state across fresh sessions in four files: agents.md (agent defs), plan.md (step checklist), progress.md (done/next), verify.md (per-step checks), so each new contextless session resumes cleanly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It comes in, it looks at progress.md. It sees what's been done before and it's like, Okay, here's where I pick up.

takeaways.what_they_do: Break tasks into small bounded goals, ban file deletion, cap max diff size, restrict to read/write, and give explicit steering ('only change this, don't touch types yet').
takeaways.evidence_quote: ban the model from deleting files, give it a max diff size ... only change this. Don't touch types yet.
